concepts.description: A cognitive system responsible for temporarily holding and manipulating information, crucial for tasks like reasoning and comprehension.
concepts.name: Working Memory

concepts.description: The system responsible for storing information over extended periods, ranging from minutes to a lifetime.
concepts.name: Long-Term Memory

concepts.description: A conceptual model that describes the three fundamental processes involved in memory formation and access: getting information in, keeping it there, and getting it back out.
concepts.name: Encoding-Storage-Retrieval Framework

concepts.description: A prominent model proposing that working memory consists of several components, including the central executive, phonological loop, and visuospatial sketchpad.
concepts.name: Baddeley's Model of Working Memory

concepts.description: A type of learning where an organism learns to associate a neutral stimulus with a meaningful stimulus, leading to a learned response.
concepts.name: Classical Conditioning

concepts.description: A type of learning in which behaviors are strengthened or weakened by the consequences that follow them, often involving reinforcement or punishment.
concepts.name: Operant Conditioning

concepts.description: A dual-process theory proposing two distinct modes of thinking: System 1 is fast, intuitive, and emotional, while System 2 is slower, more deliberate, and logical.
concepts.name: Kahneman's System 1 and System 2

concepts.description: A perceptual process where existing knowledge, expectations, and context influence how sensory information is interpreted.
concepts.name: Top-Down Perception

concepts.description: A perceptual process driven by sensory input from the environment, where raw data is processed and built up into a complete perception.
concepts.name: Bottom-Up Perception

concepts.description: Cognitive models that explain how individuals selectively focus on certain stimuli while ignoring others, influencing perception and information processing.
concepts.name: Theories of Attention

concepts.description: A metaphor suggesting that attention works like a spotlight, highlighting a specific area of interest and processing information within that focused region more thoroughly.
concepts.name: Spotlight Model of Attention

concepts.description: A model proposing that attention can be flexibly adjusted, either narrowing to intensely focus on a small area or widening to encompass a broader region with less detail.
concepts.name: Zoom Lens Model of Attention
